bibl.title: "We are the Best, We are One, and We are Greeks!" Reflections on the Ptolemies' Participation in the agones.
bibl.seg: Lukas Kainz, "We are the Best, We are One, and We are Greeks!" Reflections on the Ptolemies' Participation in the agones.
Christian Mann, Sofie Remijsen & Sebastian Scharff (edd.), Athletics in the Hellenistic World (Stuttgart, 2016) pp. 331-355.
bibl.note: Tries to explain because of which special circumstances the Ptolemies displayed more enthusiasm for these contests than other Hellenistic dynasties. The main focus lies on the times of Ptolemy II, as the most significant sources date from that time. It is argued that participation in the agones provided the kings with a good opportunity to present themselves to the Greek world as successful rulers and their whole family as a victorious unity. To explain the difference between the Ptolemies, the Antigonids and the Seleucids, it is further proposed to consider also the discourse on the ethnicity of the Ptolemies, which seems to have left its mark on the sources.
